For all calls to version() the reference contract returns the non-empty string "1.0.0" (i.e., a non-empty bytes length), whereas the mutant returns an empty string for some inputs, so the general rule is: version() must return a non-empty string; the bug breaks this by returning the empty string for at least some call.

For every call to version(), the reference contract always returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string (e.g. "1.0.1") for some input, so the returned string equality to "1.0.0" is the invariant the reference satisfies and the mutant breaks.

For every call to version(), the reference contract always returns the string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string for some input (e.g. it returns "1.1.0"), so asserting the exact returned bytes matches "1.0.0" distinguishes them.

For every call, the deployed reference contract C.version() returns the exact semantic version string "1.0.0"; the mutant returns a different string (e.g. "1.0.0-alpha") for some inputs, breaking the equality property.

property_summary: Only calls from the depositor address (DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT) are allowed to successfully invoke setL1BlockValues (calls from other addresses must revert).
The call to c.setL1BlockValues reverts exactly when the supplied caller address is not equal to c.DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT().

For any inputs and when called by the depositor account, the correct contract stores the provided `_number` into `number` (c.number() == _number); the mutant that always assigns zero breaks this by making c.number() != _number for some inputs.

For every input to setL1BlockValues, the stored `number` equals the provided `_number` (i.e. c.number() == _number); the mutant increments the stored number and thus for some _number values this equality is violated.

For every call to setL1BlockValues with an input _number, the deployed reference contract stores number == _number; the mutant decrements the stored number (wraps), so for some fuzzed _number the stored number != _number and the property fails.

For any caller address and any inputs, calling setL1BlockValues from the depositor account updates c.number to the provided _number; the mutant requiring address(0) breaks this because calls from the real depositor will not update number.

For any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the contract stores the provided _timestamp into the public timestamp field; the mutant instead overwrites timestamp with block.timestamp, so when _timestamp != block.timestamp the mutant's timestamp differs.

For any call to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract stores the provided _timestamp into the public timestamp field; the mutant ignores the argument and sets timestamp to zero, so there exist inputs where stored timestamp != supplied _timestamp.

For any inputs passed to setL1BlockValues by the depositor account, the contract stores basefee equal to the provided _basefee; the mutant which stores _basefee+1 violates this rule for inputs where _basefee does not equal _basefee+1 (i.e. any input).

For any input to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract stores the provided _basefee into the public basefee getter (c.basefee() == _basefee); the mutant always stores 0 instead, so for any nonzero _basefee the mutant violates this property.

For any inputs to setL1BlockValues the stored hash equals the provided _hash (i.e., c.hash() == _hash); the mutant that xors _hash with _batcherHash breaks this because it can make c.hash() != _hash for many inputs.

For any inputs to setL1BlockValues, the deployed contract stores the provided _hash into public variable hash; the mutant that assigns hash = _batcherHash breaks this rule for inputs where _hash != _batcherHash.

For every call to setL1BlockValues(...) the contract's public getter hash() is set to the provided _hash; the mutant omits assigning hash, so for some inputs (any _hash different from prior value) hash() will differ from the provided _hash and thus violate the rule.

For any call to setL1BlockValues, the contract's sequenceNumber public getter equals the provided _sequenceNumber parameter; the mutant assigns _number instead, so for inputs where _number != _sequenceNumber the mutant breaks this rule.

For every call to setL1BlockValues, the contract's public sequenceNumber equals the _sequenceNumber argument passed; the mutant assigns _number instead, so when _number != _sequenceNumber the mutant will violate this.

For any call to setL1BlockValues(...) the reference contract stores sequenceNumber exactly equal to the provided _sequenceNumber (assignment), whereas the mutant increments the previous stored value so sequenceNumber becomes previous + _sequenceNumber and thus can differ.

For any call to setL1BlockValues(...) by the depositor, the contract's sequenceNumber equals the provided _sequenceNumber (assignment); the mutant that adds to the prior stored value will violate this when the prior stored sequenceNumber != 0.

For any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the stored sequenceNumber equals the provided _sequenceNumber; the mutant that increments (sequenceNumber + _sequenceNumber) violates this when the prior stored sequenceNumber != 0.

For any input to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract stores the provided _sequenceNumber into the public sequenceNumber getter; the mutant resets sequenceNumber to 0, so for some fuzzed _sequenceNumber values (non-zero) the observed sequenceNumber will differ.

For every call to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract always stores the provided _batcherHash into batcherHash (c.batcherHash() == _batcherHash); the mutant that assigns batcherHash = _hash can cause c.batcherHash() != _batcherHash for some inputs.

After any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the batcherHash public getter equals the supplied _batcherHash; the mutant that omits assigning batcherHash can leave it unchanged and thus violate this for some inputs.

After any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the contract's batcherHash equals the passed _batcherHash parameter; the mutant instead always sets batcherHash to zero, breaking this property for any non-zero _batcherHash input.

For any input to setL1BlockValues, the correct contract stores the provided _batcherHash into batcherHash; the mutant instead sometimes sets batcherHash to zero, so there exist inputs where c.batcherHash() != bytes32(0) but the mutant would yield bytes32(0).

For any inputs to setL1BlockValues, the deployed contract's batcherHash equals the provided _batcherHash parameter; the mutant instead sets batcherHash to bytes32(uint256(_sequenceNumber)) and thus can differ for inputs where bytes32(uint256(_sequenceNumber)) != _batcherHash.
